description_en: Stone memorial pillars and medieval archaeological remains (14th-15th century).The artefacts presented here are all located in the vicinity of the Nigālasainī Bhagavatī Mandira, located in the village of Dehīmāṇḍau. Dehīmāṇḍau is located in a small settlement along the road between Gothalapani in the north-west and Patan in the south-east.Along the surveyed artefacts are elements of a least oneśikharatemple (BTD0020-001), a stone lion (002) and three inscribed stone memorial pillars (003 and 004). The dimensions of these objects are as follow:- stone lion, BTD0020-002: 70 x 90 x 25 cm- memorial pillar, BTD0020-003: 109 x 41 x 39 cm- memorial pillar, BTD0020-004: 101 x 34 x 35 cm- memorial pillar, BTD0020-005: 85 x 36 x 35 cmThe pillars are dated but the content of the inscriptions remains mostly unclear, except for pillar 004, where one may read the date of ŚS 1309 (1387 CE). This period corresponds to the rule of Nāga Malla Deva, the king of Doti. Each pillar has a niche in which is carved a foot warrior (003 and 005) or a horse rider (004).D. R. Sharma mentions two pillars (Sharma 2012: 350-351).
references: Sources and references Inscription identification number BTD0020_I_001

historical_events.event_name: Installation of pillar BTD0020-003 in ca. late 14th century
historical_events.event_description: The southern side of the pillar contains adevanāgarīinscription of seven lines. It remains difficult to read the inscription. Owing to the stylistical ressemblance between this pillar and the others from the site that are dated of ŚS 1309 (1387 CE), it may be suggested that this pillar was installed around the same time period, i.e., the late 14th century,The inscription is less well executed than on the other pillars.

historical_events.event_name: Installation of pillar BTD0020-004 in 1387 CE
historical_events.event_description: Pillar BTD0020-004 contains an inscription of three lines indevanāgarīscript. According to D. R. Sharma the reading of the inscription is as follows:Śri sāke 1309 bāghi kot vadā likhitam...gutahatranslated as: "In saka [śaka] 1309 this... is written by Vadā from Bāghikot" (Sharma 2012: 350).

historical_events.event_name: Installation of pillar BTD0020-005 in 1387 CE
historical_events.event_description: Pillar BTD0020-005 contains an inscription of three lines indevanāgarīscript. According to D. R. Sharma, one may only read the date ofśaka1309 (1387 CE). This reading makes the pillar contemporaneous to BTD0020-004 (Sharma 2012: 351).
